   176	public:
   177	    using FusedCompletionFn = void (*)(void*, Client*);
   178	
   179	    WbEngine& engine() { return wb_; }
   180	    bool init(Server* srv, ThreadCtx* self, bool dormant = false) {
   181	        srv_ = srv; self_ = self;
   182	        aof_manager_ = srv->aof().configured() ? &srv->aof() : nullptr;
   183	        foreign_touch_random_ ^= (static_cast<uint64_t>(self->id()) + 1) * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
   184	        lb_sample_rate_ = srv->key_lb_signals_enabled() ? srv->lb_sample_rate() : 0;
   185	        lb_sample_countdown_ = lb_sample_rate_;
   186	        lb_controller_armed_ = srv->key_lb_signals_enabled();
   187	        age_sample_rate_cached_ = srv->effective_age_sample_rate();
   188	        ex_sched_enabled_ = srv->cfg().ex_sched != 0;
   189	        pipeline_batches_ = Fused && srv->cfg().overlap != 0;
   190	        // Both interwoven schedules use the proven iofused fixed producer lanes.  The legacy
   191	        // streams implementation remains in this file for branch comparison, but overlap 2 no
   192	        // longer reaches its reservation-aware task transport.
   193	        iofused_ = Fused && srv->cfg().overlap != 0;
   194	        if constexpr (Fused) {
   195	            if (srv->read_local_enabled()) {
   196	                std::unique_ptr<ReadLocalExImpl> impl(new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalExImpl);
   197	                if (!impl) return false;
   198	                impl->lane.reset(new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalExImpl::LaneEntry[kInboxSlots]);
   199	                impl->lane_fallbacks.reset(
   200	                    new (std::nothrow) ReadLocalFallbackReason[kInboxSlots]);
   201	                if (!impl->lane || !impl->lane_fallbacks ||
   202	                    !impl->deferred.init(srv, self)) return false;
   203	                impl->point_writes_precise =
   204	                    srv->cfg().maxmemory == 0 ||
   205	                    srv->cfg().maxmemory_policy == MaxmemoryPolicy::NoEviction;
   206	                read_local_.impl = std::move(impl);
   207	            }
   208	        }
   209	        if (!ring_.init(1024)) return false;
   210	        fused_handoff_ring_ = &ring_;
   211	        wb_.bind(&ring_);
   212	        initialized_ = true;
   213	        if (!dormant) activate();
   214	        return true;
   215	    }
   216	
   217	    void activate() {
   218	        if (!initialized_) std::abort();
   219	        self_->set_ring(&ring_);
   220	        self_->set_wb_engine(nullptr);
   221	        blocking_bind_executor(srv_, self_, &ring_);
   222	        for (Shard* shard : self_->shards())
   223	            shard->bind_notify_pending(&notify_keyless_pending_);
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    // Fused tenure shares the physical thread with IoLoop. IoLoop remains the published wake
   227	    // endpoint because it owns the only blocking wait; this ring still carries persistence CQEs.
   228	    void activate_fused(Ring* handoff_ring) {
   229	        static_assert(Fused);
   230	        if (!initialized_) std::abort();
   231	        // Interwoven schedules put executor-originated task/client handoffs on the network ring.
   232	        // That leaves this private ring with control/persistence SQEs; both iofused-family arms
   233	        // amortize at their shared N2 boundary. Pipeline 0 retains its existing ring ownership.
   234	        if (srv_->cfg().overlap != 0 && handoff_ring)
   235	            fused_handoff_ring_ = handoff_ring;

   527	              uint8_t Pipeline = 0>
   528	    void run_loop() {
   529	        static_assert(Pipeline <= 2);
   530	        if constexpr (Fused && Pipeline == 1) {
   531	            run_fused_iofused_loop<HasUnix, HasTls, kEp, false>();
   532	            return;
   533	        }
   534	        if constexpr (Fused && Pipeline == 2) {
   535	            // Overlap 2 is the gated three-way extension of iofused.  The old streams loop remains
   536	            // below for branch comparison, but no boot-time dispatch can reach it.
   537	            run_fused_iofused_loop<HasUnix, HasTls, kEp, true>();
   538	            return;
   539	        }
   540	        constexpr bool IoPipe = !Fused && Pipeline == 1;
   541	        if constexpr (!kEp) {
   542	            if (listen_fd_ >= 0) arm_accept(UrKind::Accept);
   543	            if constexpr (HasTls) arm_accept(UrKind::TlsAccept);
   544	            if constexpr (HasUnix) if (unix_listen_fd_ >= 0) arm_accept(UrKind::UnixAccept);
   545	        }
   546	        LoopSignals& sig = self_->sig();
   547	        while (!self_->stop_flag().load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
   548	               self_->role() == Role::Ifid) {
   549	            refresh_notify_config();
   550	            // ONE relaxed load per io batch. Per-batch checks are free; this is what buys the
   551	            // per-operation hooks their zero-cost-when-off property.
   552	            if (__builtin_expect(srv_->climon_armed() != climon_armed_cached_, false))
   553	                climon_refresh_armed();
   554	            const bool pause_armed = climon_pause_armed();
   555	            const bool client_cron_armed = !srv_->flip_dispatch_paused() &&
   556	                                           srv_->client_cron_armed();
   557	            const bool client_lb_signal_armed = client_lb_signal_armed_;
   558	            const bool lb_controller_armed = lb_controller_armed_;
   559	            // Placement's dense role vectors are mutated only under FLIP's global dispatch
   560	            // barrier. Do not consult them from an IO pass while that cold transaction is live.
   561	            const bool save_cron_armed = !srv_->flip_dispatch_paused() &&
   562	                                         srv_->save_cron_writer(self_->id());
   563	            const bool client_cron_newly_armed = client_cron_armed && !client_cron_was_armed_;
   564	            if (!client_cron_armed && __builtin_expect(client_cron_was_armed_, false)) {
   565	                // Turning the last client cron consumer off also retires output accounting once.
   566	                // The disabled write-back specialization then has no per-serve cleanup branch.
   567	                for (Client* c : self_->clients()) c->stop_obuf_tracking();
   568	            }

    39	void IoLoop::run_fused() {
    40	    if (!fused_executor_) std::abort();
    41	    const bool has_unix = unix_listen_fd_ >= 0 ||
    42	                          (srv_->cfg().unixsocket && *srv_->cfg().unixsocket);
    43	    auto run_pipeline = [&](auto pipeline_tag) {
    44	        constexpr uint8_t Pipeline = decltype(pipeline_tag)::value;
    45	        if (epoll_) {
    46	            if (tls_context_) {
    47	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    48	                else run_loop<false, true, true, true, Pipeline>();
    49	            } else {
    50	                if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    51	                else run_loop<false, false, true, true, Pipeline>();
    52	            }
    53	            return;
    54	        }
    55	        if (tls_context_) {
    56	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    57	            else run_loop<false, true, false, true, Pipeline>();
    58	        } else {
    59	            if (has_unix) run_loop<true, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    60	            else run_loop<false, false, false, true, Pipeline>();
    61	        }
    62	    };
    63	    switch (srv_->cfg().overlap) {
    64	        case 0: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 0>{}); break;
    65	        case 1: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 1>{}); break;
    66	        case 2: run_pipeline(std::integral_constant<uint8_t, 2>{}); break;
    67	        default: std::abort();
    68	    }
    69	}

    71	int run_fused_server(Server& srv, const SnapshotLoadPlan* aof_base_plan,
    72	                     const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<AofReplayPlan>>& aof_plans,
    73	                     const SnapshotLoadPlan* load_plan, TlsContext* tls_context,
    74	                     LateUnixListener& unix_listener,
    75	                     ShutdownReportFinalLine& final_report) {
    76	    const Config& cfg = srv.cfg();
    77	    const uint32_t nthreads = srv.nthreads();
    78	    std::printf("tomokv-cpp: %u unified threads, %u shard(s), thread-mode=1s,"
    79	                " overlap=%u, %s, alloc=%s\n", nthreads, cfg.shards,
    80	                cfg.overlap,
    81	                cfg.net_io == NetIoEngine::Epoll ? "epoll" : "io_uring", alloc_backend());
    82	    for (const ThreadPlacement& placement : srv.placement().threads())
    83	        std::printf("  thread t%u: role=unified cpu=%d L3=%u shards=%zu send=self\n",
    84	                    placement.id, placement.cpu, placement.domain,
    85	                    srv.thread(placement.id).shards().size());
    86	    std::fflush(stdout);
    87	
    88	    std::vector<std::thread> pool;
    89	    std::vector<IoLoop> ios(nthreads);

  1923	    // branch; an unoptimized assertion build retains the diagnostic check.
  1924	    uint32_t worker_of_shard(int32_t shard_id) const {
  1925	#if !defined(NDEBUG) && !defined(__OPTIMIZE__)
  1926	        if (shard_id < 0 || static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) >= shards_.size()) std::abort();
  1927	#endif
  1928	        return shard_owner_[shard_id].load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  1929	    }
  1930	    void set_worker_of_shard(int32_t shard_id, uint32_t thread_id) {
  1931	        if (shard_id < 0 || static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) >= shards_.size()) std::abort();
  1932	        Shard& sh = *shards_[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id)];
  1933	        router_.set_initial_owner(sh.bucket_begin(), sh.bucket_end(), thread_id);
  1934	        shard_owner_[shard_id].store(thread_id, std::memory_order_release);
  1935	    }
  1936	
  1937	    // The caller must hold both executor loops at the safe point described in NOTES-MIGRATE.md:
  1938	    // no executing/retry/group/snapshot work may touch this shard.  Queue entries which arrive via
  1939	    // a stale pre-commit route are harmless because ExLoop rechecks and forwards before access.
  1940	    // Vector capacity and membership are settled while PREPARING still names the source.  The
  1941	    // phase store in commit_transfer() is the sole ownership edge; bucket entries and the derived
  1942	    // shard array publish destination only after that edge.
  1943	    // THE OWNERSHIP EDGE OWNS THE SINK.
  1944	    //
  1945	    // A shard's read-local retire sink names TWO structures that belong to one thread and are
  1946	    // protected by nothing else: the owner's QSBR retire ring (`defer`, a single-producer ring) and
  1947	    // the owner's private block cache (`block_cache`, an unlocked free list). Every armed write on
  1948	    // the shard reaches both through the shard's store, so the sink must name the thread that is
  1949	    // executing that shard's writes -- at every instant, not eventually.
  1950	    //
  1951	    // Moving the shard without moving the sink leaves the DESTINATION executing writes through the
  1952	    // SOURCE's ring and free list. Two threads then splice one unlocked list: the loser's update is
  1953	    // lost, a block ends up linked twice, and the damage surfaces later as either
  1954	    // KvBlockCache::put's `heads[cls] == memory` abort or a take() of a still-linked block whose
  1955	    // KvObj header overwrites the list `next`, so that the NEXT take dereferences a wild pointer.
  1956	    // Both were observed (see DESIGN-P0REPLY.md).
  1957	    //
  1958	    // The rebind used to be deferred to the destination's own next executor pass
  1959	    // (`lb_rebind_pending_` -> `read_local_rebind_owned_shards_after_lb`). Nothing ordered that
  1960	    // pass before the destination's first write to the shard it had just been given, and the
  1961	    // reproduction shows exactly that gap: transfer sid 1 to thread 1, then thread 1 executing
  1962	    // cmd_set on it against thread 7's cache, with no rebind in between.
  1963	    //
  1964	    // Here there is no gap. Both callers hold every executor at the quiesced safe point (the LB
  1965	    // commits only once every EX thread has acked ExDrain, which `flip_quiesced()` grants only with
  1966	    // an EMPTY retire ring), so the source has nothing outstanding for this shard and the
  1967	    // destination has not started. The sink moves with ownership, in the same critical section.
  1968	    void adopt_read_local_retire_sink(Shard& shard, uint32_t destination) {
  1969	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_NO_EAGER_ADOPT
  1970	        // NEGATIVE CONTROL (Makefile target `rlcache-nofix`): restores the pre-fix behaviour, where
  1971	        // the sink was left for the destination's own later pass to rebind. Every invariant added
  1972	        // for this defect MUST fail against this build; a detector that cannot report failure
  1973	        // proves nothing about the runs that pass.
  1974	        (void)shard; (void)destination;
  1975	        return;
  1976	#else
  1977	        if (!shard.store().read_local_enabled()) return;
  1978	        const ReadLocalRetireSink* sink = threads_[destination]->read_local_retire_sink_or_null();
  1979	        if (!sink) std::abort();
  1980	        shard.store().rebind_read_local_retire_sink(*sink);

   332	    void collapse_empty() {
   333	        if (!rehashing() && cap_[0] <= kMinCap) {
   334	            std::memset(states(0), kEmpty, cap_[0]);
   335	            tombs_[0] = 0;
   336	            cursor_ = 0;
   337	            return;
   338	        }
   339	        release(0);
   340	        release(1);
   341	        cursor_ = 0;
   342	        migrate_ = 0;
   343	    }
   344	
   345	    bool begin_rehash(size_t cap) {
   346	        if (!allocate(1, cap)) return false;
   347	        migrate_ = 0;
   348	        return true;
   349	    }
   350	
   351	    // A moved slot becomes a TOMBSTONE, never kEmpty: the old table is still being probed by
   352	    // erase_in() while the move runs, and kEmpty terminates a probe run. Punching holes made a
   353	    // still-present deadline unfindable, which showed up as INFO `expires` over-reporting after
   354	    // PERSIST.
   355	    void migrate(uint32_t slots) {
   356	        while (slots && migrate_ < cap_[0]) {
   357	            const size_t pos = migrate_++;
   358	            slots--;
   359	            if (states(0)[pos] != kLive) continue;
   360	            const int64_t deadline = kTtlDeadlineSidecar ? deadlines(0)[pos] : kNoTtlDeadline;
   361	            states(0)[pos] = kTomb;
   362	            live_[0]--;
   363	            tombs_[0]++;
   364	            // Cannot fail: the destination was sized for every live entry plus headroom.
   365	            (void)insert_raw(1, hashes_[0][pos], deadline);
   366	        }
   367	        if (migrate_ >= cap_[0]) finish_migration();
   368	    }
   369	
   370	    void finish_migration() {
   371	        while (migrate_ < cap_[0]) {
   372	            const size_t pos = migrate_++;
   373	            if (states(0)[pos] != kLive) continue;
   374	            const int64_t deadline = kTtlDeadlineSidecar ? deadlines(0)[pos] : kNoTtlDeadline;
   375	            states(0)[pos] = kTomb;
   376	            live_[0]--;
   377	            tombs_[0]++;
   378	            (void)insert_raw(1, hashes_[0][pos], deadline);
   379	        }
   380	        std::free(hashes_[0]);
   381	        std::free(sidecars_[0]);
   382	        hashes_[0] = hashes_[1];
   383	        sidecars_[0] = sidecars_[1];
   384	        cap_[0] = cap_[1];
   385	        live_[0] = live_[1];
   386	        tombs_[0] = tombs_[1];
   387	        hashes_[1] = nullptr;
   388	        sidecars_[1] = nullptr;
   389	        cap_[1] = 0;
   390	        live_[1] = tombs_[1] = 0;
   391	        migrate_ = 0;
   392	        cursor_ = 0;
   393	    }
   394	
   395	    size_t start(int t, uint64_t hash) const {
   396	        return static_cast<size_t>(mix64(hash)) & (cap_[t] - 1);
   397	    }
   398	
   399	    bool insert_raw(int t, uint64_t hash, int64_t deadline) {
   400	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   401	        if (!cap) return false;
   402	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   403	        size_t first_tomb = cap;
   404	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   405	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) {
   406	                if (first_tomb != cap) { pos = first_tomb; tombs_[t]--; }
   407	                hashes_[t][pos] = hash;
   408	                if constexpr (kTtlDeadlineSidecar) deadlines(t)[pos] = deadline;
   409	                states(t)[pos] = kLive;
   410	                live_[t]++;
   411	                return true;
   412	            }
   413	            if (states(t)[pos] == kTomb) {
   414	                if (first_tomb == cap) first_tomb = pos;
   415	            } else if (hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   416	                if constexpr (kTtlDeadlineSidecar) deadlines(t)[pos] = deadline;
   417	                return true;
   418	            }
   419	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   420	        }
   421	        return false;
   422	    }
   423	
   424	    bool erase_in(int t, uint64_t hash) {
   425	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   426	        if (!cap) return false;
   427	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   428	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   429	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) return false;
   430	            if (states(t)[pos] == kLive && hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   431	                states(t)[pos] = kTomb;
   432	                live_[t]--;
   433	                tombs_[t]++;
   434	                return true;
   435	            }
   436	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   437	        }
   438	        return false;
   439	    }
   440	
   441	    bool deadline_in(int t, uint64_t hash, int64_t& out) const {
   442	        if constexpr (!kTtlDeadlineSidecar) return false;
   443	        const size_t cap = cap_[t];
   444	        if (!cap) return false;
   445	        size_t pos = start(t, hash);
   446	        for (size_t probes = 0; probes < cap; probes++) {
   447	            if (states(t)[pos] == kEmpty) return false;
   448	            if (states(t)[pos] == kLive && hashes_[t][pos] == hash) {
   449	                out = deadlines(t)[pos];
   450	                return true;
   451	            }
   452	            pos = (pos + 1) & (cap - 1);
   453	        }
   454	        return false;
   455	    }

   460	    uint32_t  live_[2]   = {0, 0};

   462	    size_t    cursor_ = 0;    // sampling cursor over the concatenation of both tables
   463	    size_t    migrate_ = 0;   // next old-table slot to move while a migration is in flight
   464	};

   185	    // Covers every unsealed entry with `stamp` as one batch. Returns how many were sealed.
   186	    uint32_t seal(uint64_t stamp) {
   187	        const uint32_t sealed = unsealed;
   188	        if (!sealed) return 0;
   189	        if (batch_count == kBatchCapacity) {
   190	            Batch& newest = batches[(batch_head + batch_count - 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   191	            newest.stamp = stamp;
   192	            newest.count += sealed;
   193	        } else {
   194	            Batch& batch = batches[(batch_head + batch_count) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   195	            batch.stamp = stamp;
   196	            batch.count = sealed;
   197	            batch_count++;
   198	        }
   199	        unsealed = 0;
   200	        return sealed;
   201	    }
   202	
   203	    // Pops every sealed batch whose stamp is below `floor`, oldest first, handing each entry slot
   204	    // to `fn` in retirement order. Batches are FIFO with non-decreasing stamps, so the first batch
   205	    // at or above the floor ends the drain exactly where a per-entry test would. Unsealed entries
   206	    // are never popped here.
   207	    template <typename Fn>
   208	    uint32_t drain_below(uint64_t floor, Fn&& fn) {
   209	        uint32_t drained = 0;
   210	        while (batch_count) {
   211	            const Batch& batch = batches[batch_head];
   212	            if (batch.stamp >= floor) break;
   213	            for (uint32_t remaining = batch.count; remaining; remaining--) {
   214	                fn(head);
   215	                head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   216	            }
   217	            count -= batch.count;
   218	            drained += batch.count;
   219	            batch_head = (batch_head + 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1);
   220	            batch_count--;
   221	        }
   222	        return drained;
   223	    }
   224	
   225	    // Pops everything, sealed or not. Only valid once no reader can retain a pointer (shutdown).
   226	    template <typename Fn>
   227	    uint32_t drain_all(Fn&& fn) {
   228	        const uint32_t drained = count;
   229	        while (count) {
   230	            fn(head);
   231	            head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   232	            count--;
   233	        }
   234	        unsealed = 0;
   235	        batch_head = 0;
   236	        batch_count = 0;
   237	        return drained;
   238	    }

  3343	    void atomic_reconfigure_credits(uint32_t window) {

  3352	                continue;
  3353	            }

  3355	                    generation, generation + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
  3356	                    std::memory_order_acquire))

  3364	            AtomicAdmissionLease& lease = thread(io).atomic_admission_lease();

  3370	        const uint64_t bounded = std::min<uint64_t>(active, UINT32_MAX);
  3371	        atomic_credit_pool_.store(
  3372	            window && bounded < window ? window - static_cast<uint32_t>(bounded) : 0,
  3373	            std::memory_order_release);

  3375	            window && bounded > window ? static_cast<uint32_t>(bounded - window) : 0,

  1135	                lb_fold_signals();

  1556	    // turn each 32-operation chunk into a scan of the 1024-entry lane.
  1557	    template <bool YieldToOwner = false>
  1558	    uint32_t drain_local_reads_bounded(uint32_t op_budget) {
  1559	        if constexpr (!Fused) {
  1560	            return 0;
  1561	        } else {
  1562	            if (!read_local_enabled() || !op_budget) return 0;
  1563	            return drain_local_reads_bounded_impl<true, YieldToOwner>(op_budget);
  1564	        }
  1565	    }
  1566	
  1567	    template <bool CapturePrefetch, bool YieldToOwner>
  1568	    uint32_t drain_local_reads_bounded_impl(uint32_t op_budget) {
  1569	        static_assert(Fused);
  1570	        auto& lane = read_local_impl();
  1571	        if (!lane.lane_count) return 0;
  1572	        // One record per chunk entry. Gather resolves the Op, its home store and its MGET class
  1573	        // exactly once; every later pass reads them from here instead of walking the ROB again.
  1574	        // Stack-local to this bounded drain, so nothing here outlives the rotation's QSBR tick.
  1575	        struct LocalReadChunk {
  1576	            Op* ops[kReadLocalDrainChunkOps];
  1577	            FlatStore* stores[kReadLocalDrainChunkOps];   // null for an MGET (multi-store)
  1578	            uint64_t op_ids[kReadLocalDrainChunkOps];
  1579	            ReadLocalFallbackReason fallbacks[kReadLocalDrainChunkOps];
  1580	        } chunk;
  1581	        static_assert(kReadLocalDrainChunkOps <= 32, "mget_mask is one 32-bit word");
  1582	        [[maybe_unused]] ReadLocalCaptureBuffer<
  1583	            CapturePrefetch, kReadLocalDrainChunkOps> captures;
  1584	        const uint32_t nshards = srv_->nshards();
  1585	        ReadLocalStats& stats = self_->read_local_stats();
  1586	        uint32_t work = 0;
  1587	        uint32_t consumed = 0;
  1588	        auto discard_tombstone_heads = [&] {
  1589	            while (lane.lane_count) {
  1590	                const auto& head = lane.lane[lane.lane_head];
  1591	                if (head.client && head.client->rob().pending_read_local(head.op_id)) break;
  1592	                lane.lane_head = (lane.lane_head + 1) & (kInboxSlots - 1);
  1593	                lane.lane_count--;
  1594	            }
  1595	        };
  1596	        auto owner_turn_pending = [&] {
  1597	            if constexpr (YieldToOwner) {
  1598	                if (!consumed || consumed % kReadLocalDrainChunkOps) return false;
  1599	                return fairlane_owner_debt_pending() ||
  1600	                    self_->notified_task_depth_capped(1) != 0;
  1601	            }
  1602	            return false;
  1603	        };
  1604	        // Work through each client's lane run in gather/prefetch-sized chunks. A successful chunk
  1605	        // can commit immediately. At a fallback, only the intrinsically failing entries and their
  1606	        // transitive same-key set move in a ROB-ordered owner wave; unrelated reads remain local.
  1607	        discard_tombstone_heads();
  1608	        while (lane.lane_count && consumed < op_budget) {
  1609	            const auto& head = lane.lane[lane.lane_head];
  1610	            Client* client = head.client;
  1611	            auto& rob = client->rob();
  1612	            uint32_t count = 0;
  1613	            uint32_t capacity = std::min<uint32_t>(
  1614	                kReadLocalDrainChunkOps, op_budget - consumed);
  1615	            if constexpr (YieldToOwner)
  1616	                capacity = std::min<uint32_t>(
  1617	                    capacity, kReadLocalDrainChunkOps -
  1618	                        consumed % kReadLocalDrainChunkOps);
  1619	            // Gather: one ROB frontier snapshot for the whole same-client run (see
  1620	            // Rob::pending_read_local(id, dispatch, flush)), and each entry's Op, home store and
  1621	            // MGET class resolved here once. bit i of mget_mask marks an MGET entry.
  1622	            const uint64_t dispatch = rob.dispatch_id();
  1623	            const uint64_t flush = rob.flush_id();
  1624	            uint32_t mget_mask = 0;
  1625	            while (count < lane.lane_count && count < capacity) {
  1626	                const uint32_t index =
  1627	                    (lane.lane_head + count) & (kInboxSlots - 1);
  1628	                const auto& task = lane.lane[index];
  1629	                if (task.client != client ||
  1630	                    !rob.pending_read_local(task.op_id, dispatch, flush))
  1631	                    break;
  1632	                Op& op = rob.at(task.op_id);
  1633	                const bool mget = read_local_mget(op);
  1634	                if (!mget && op.shard < 0) std::abort();
  1635	                chunk.ops[count] = &op;
  1636	                chunk.stores[count] = mget ? nullptr : &srv_->shard(op.shard).store();
  1637	                chunk.op_ids[count] = task.op_id;
  1638	                chunk.fallbacks[count] = lane.lane_fallbacks[index];
  1639	                mget_mask |= uint32_t{mget} << count;
  1640	                count++;
  1641	            }
  1642	            if (!count) std::abort();
  1643	            consumed += count;
  1644	
  1645	            // Pure point chunks retain the widest I0/C0/E0 overlap. A mixed chunk captures and
  1646	            // consumes each command in program order below: MGET may retry and recapture, so
  1647	            // pre-capturing a following GET could otherwise let that later command regress.
  1648	            [[maybe_unused]] const bool point_capture_batch = CapturePrefetch && mget_mask == 0;
  1649	
  1650	            if constexpr (CapturePrefetch) {
  1651	                if (point_capture_batch) {
  1652	                    // I0 retains the old whole-batch home-slot overlap. C0 consumes those warm
  1653	                    // words, records their decoded objects, and hints object/value bytes for E0.
  1654	                    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
  1655	                        chunk.stores[i]->read_local_prefetch(chunk.ops[i]->hash);
  1656	                    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
  1657	                        const Op& op = *chunk.ops[i];
  1658	                        captures.entries[i] =
  1659	                            chunk.stores[i]->read_local_prefetch_capture(op.hash, op.key());
  1660	                    }
  1661	                }
  1662	            } else {
  1663	                // Selector 0 is the original hint-only path, including MGET's established bounded
  1664	                // prefetch inside prepare_local_mget().
  1665	                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
  1666	                    if (!((mget_mask >> i) & 1u))
  1667	                        chunk.stores[i]->read_local_prefetch(chunk.ops[i]->hash);
  1668	            }
  5545	                pubsub_work += pubsub_drain_events();
  5546	                return;
  5547	            }
  5548	            // AF_UNIX accept handoffs use this existing channel without claiming retirement.
  5549	            // Executor completions always CAS retire_queued false->true before posting, so the bit
  5550	            // distinguishes the two meanings without adding a Client field or a catalog lock here.
  5551	            if constexpr (HasUnix)
  5552	                if (!c->retire_queued().load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
  5553	                    adopt_client<kEp>(c, true);
  5554	                    if constexpr (TargetedIfid) enqueue_ifid(c);
  5555	                    return;
  5556	                }
  5557	            c->retire_queued().store(false, std::memory_order_release);
  5558	            enqueue_serve(c);                    // a posted client is a serve request
  5559	            mark_active_known<TargetedIfid>(c);
  5560	        };
  5561	        uint32_t n = unmasked ? self_->drain_clients_unmasked(take) : self_->drain_clients(take);
  5562	        // The ready-mask path: workers set one bit per completed-work burst; we map slot -> client,
  5563	        // flag it FOR SERVING, and put it back in the active set. The flag is the point: serving
  5564	        // every active conn every pass measured 93% EMPTY serves at 8 nodes -- 526M drain-checks
  5565	        // that each pulled a remote worker's cache line to learn there was nothing to do. Targeted
  5566	        // serving turns the poll into a response.
  5567	        for (uint32_t w = 0; w < ReadyMask::kWords; w++) {
  5568	            uint64_t bits = self_->ready().take(w);
  5569	            while (bits) {
  5570	                const uint32_t b = static_cast<uint32_t>(__builtin_ctzll(bits));
  5571	                bits &= bits - 1;
  5572	                Client* c = self_->wb_slot_client(w * 64 + b);
  5573	                if (c && !c->dead()) {
  5574	                    enqueue_serve(c);
  5575	                    mark_active_known<TargetedIfid>(c);
  5576	                    n++;
  5577	                }
  5578	            }
  5579	        }
  5580	        return n + pubsub_work;
  5581	    }
  5582	
  5583	    bool client_pipeline_referenced(const Client* client) const {
  5584	        if (client->ifid_pending()) return true;
  5585	        if (active_ifid_context_)
  5586	            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < active_ifid_context_->count; i++)
  5587	                if (active_ifid_context_->entries[i].client == client) return true;
  5588	        if (active_wb_context_)
  5589	            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < active_wb_context_->count; i++)
  5590	                if (active_wb_context_->clients[i] == client) return true;
  5591	        return false;
  5592	    }
  5593	
  5594	    bool io_pipelines_quiesced() const {
  5595	        return active_ifid_context_ == nullptr && active_wb_context_ == nullptr;
  5596	    }

   704	    // ---- the ONLY cross-thread fields ----------------------------------------------------------
   705	    // A connection may be freed only when (a) nothing is in flight through its ROB AND (b) no
   706	    // Client* naming it can still surface from a notification channel. (b) is what the ASAN
   707	    // use-after-free proved: a worker posts the client for retirement, io serves it through
   708	    // flush_ready instead, the ROB quiesces, the peer disconnects, close frees the client -- and
   709	    // io then drains its channel into freed memory. The claim flag covers every CLAIMED post: it is
   710	    // set before posting and cleared only when the consumer takes the entry, and after quiescence
   711	    // no new claim can ever be made (no op will complete again), so requiring it false here is
   712	    // race-free.

   715	               !pipeline_prepared() &&
   716	               !recv_armed_ && !send_inflight_ &&        // the KERNEL holds no pointer into us
   717	               !retire_queued_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
   718	               watched_refs_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;

   724	               !send_inflight_ && !serve_pending_ &&
   725	               !retire_queued_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&
   726	               watched_refs_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0 &&
   727	               barrier_owners_ == 0 && atomic_groups_io_ == 0 && !blocked() &&

   735	               !send_inflight_ && !serve_pending_ &&
   736	               !retire_queued_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) &&

   741	    // Set by a worker before it tells the owning IO thread this client has ops to retire; cleared by
   742	    // that IO thread when it picks the client up. Without it, a pipelined burst of N completions
   743	    // enqueues the same client N times and the retire channel fills with duplicates.
    19	// WHAT CROSSES THREADS, in pure 2s: the io thread owns BOTH counters (it parses and it retires).
    20	// The executor only ever touches individual Op slots — reached through chunk pointers published
    21	// with release/acquire, contents ordered by the Op's own state handshake (Issued/Done). The two
    22	// counters stay atomics anyway: on x86 the same-thread case degrades to ordinary loads and stores
    23	// (zero cost), and dispatch_id == flush_id is the quiescence fence a future connection MIGRATION
    24	// between io threads must read from the other side — demoting them buys nothing and closes a door.
    25	//
    26	// READ-BUFFER PINNING STILL FALLS OUT. argv Slices point into the connection's read buffer. Because
    27	// retirement is strictly in order, the oldest live op is always slot(flush_id) — so every byte
    28	// before that op's rbuf_off is dead. No refcounting, no generation numbers.
    29	//
    30	// SLOTS ARE CHUNKED, NOT INLINE AND NOT SCATTERED. An ExecContext is ~328 bytes; held by value a
    31	// 64-slot ROB is ~21KB resident per connection whether it ever pipelines or not. The first pointer
    32	// version fixed that with one heap Op per slot — and measured a −3% SET p32 regression, because 64
    33	// scattered allocations lost the sequential locality the drain used to get from the inline array
    34	// for free. So: contexts materialize in CONTIGUOUS CHUNKS of eight, on the first touch of any slot
    35	// in the chunk. A p1 connection holds one chunk (~2.6KB), a 32-deep pipeliner four, and the drain
    36	// walks sequential memory within every chunk. Each context recycles in place forever ("flushed"
    37	// logically at retire — state goes Free — never returned to the allocator until the connection
    38	// dies); steady-state allocator traffic is zero, and jemalloc needs no pool in front of it.
    39	#pragma once
    40	#include <atomic>
    41	#include <cstdint>
    42	#include <cstdlib>
    43	#include <new>
    44	#include "../exec/op.h"

    46	namespace tomo {

    48	// THE ROB WINDOW: the maximum number of ops one connection may have in flight. It lives here,
    49	// in the ROB's own header, because it is the ROB's bound and because the read-local write ring
    50	// below is sized FROM it -- one number, so the ring can never drift out of step with the window
    51	// its unreachability proof is written against. net/conn.h re-exports it by including this file.
    52	inline constexpr uint32_t kRobWindow = 64;   // max in-flight ops per connection
    53	
    54	// COLD-PATH COUNTERS FOR ARM-ON-DEMAND (DESIGN-RINGDIET.md). Three events, none of them on a hot
    55	// path: a connection being armed, its RYOW sidecar being allocated, and one write being committed
    56	// into the ring. They are the instrument the design is proved with -- "pure SET does zero ring
    57	// bookkeeping" is exactly write_ring_records staying at zero -- so they are always on rather than
    58	// diagnostic-only, which is affordable precisely because every increment sits behind a noinline
    59	// call that the unarmed stream never makes. The ROB holds a POINTER to the owning IO thread's
    60	// block (installed at adopt and re-pointed at the migration edge) so that net/ need not know what
    61	// a ThreadCtx is; core/thread.h embeds one by value inside ReadLocalStats.
    62	struct ReadLocalArmStats {
    63	    uint64_t arms = 0;                  // connections a local read armed
    64	    uint64_t sidecars = 0;              // RYOW write-ring sidecars allocated (never at accept)
    65	    uint64_t write_ring_records = 0;    // writes committed into the RYOW write ring
    66	};
    67	
    68	// Allocated only for connections served by the boot-armed fused read-local lane. The connection's
    69	// IO owner is the sole reader/writer; the ROB ids carried beside hashes are generations, not
    70	// cross-thread publications. Retirement is therefore lazy: flush_id advancing past an entry is
    71	// its removal fence, and stale entries may only cause an allowed false-positive conflict.
    72	struct alignas(64) ReadLocalRobState {
    73	    // SIZED TO THE ROB WINDOW, WHICH MAKES CAPACITY OVERFLOW UNREACHABLE. A ring entry is removed
    74	    // by retirement, so every live entry names an op in [flush_id, dispatch_id) -- distinct ids in
    75	    // a window that is at most kRobWindow wide. Both insert sites prune immediately before testing
    76	    // capacity, and the write being inserted holds one of those ids itself, so after the prune
    77	    // write_count <= in_flight - 1 <= kRobWindow - 1. Rob asserts kWriteRingCapacity >= Capacity,
    78	    // which is the whole argument. Measured against the instrument that does not depend on it
    79	    // (scratchpad/ringsize): a client pipelining 64 deep at 100% writes tops out at exactly 63
    80	    // live writes, one short of the window, and 41% reads at depth 32 tops out at 19.
    81	    static constexpr uint32_t kWriteRingCapacity = kRobWindow;
    82	    // A POLICY BOUND, NOT THE RING'S. How many keys a single blind MSET may name and still take a
    83	    // precise ring slot instead of a conservative generation: every probe that hits that slot walks
    84	    // the op's argv, so this trades demotions against walk length and has nothing to do with how
    85	    // many writes the ring can hold. Deliberately left where it was when the two were one number.
    86	    static constexpr uint32_t kMaxPreciseKeysetKeys = 16;
    87	    static_assert((kWriteRingCapacity & (kWriteRingCapacity - 1)) == 0);
    88	    static_assert(kWriteRingCapacity <= 64, "keyset/valid/wide slot bitmap width");
    89	    static_assert(kMaxPreciseKeysetKeys <= kWriteRingCapacity);
    90	
    91	    static constexpr uint64_t keyset_filter(uint64_t hash) {
    92	        return (uint64_t{1} << (hash & 63)) |
    93	               (uint64_t{1} << ((hash >> 32) & 63));
    94	    }

    96	    enum class PendingWrite : uint8_t { None, Hash, Keyset, Overflow };

   101	    };
   102

   428	// THE MIGRATION CONTRACT. Moving a physical shard rewrites the EX-owner bits of its bucket range
   429	// behind Router's transfer descriptor. What makes it correct is the ordering around it:
   430	//
   431	//   1. Bring the old owner to an execution safe point. task_in.quiesced() tests the RETIRED
   432	//      frontier; head == tail alone is insufficient because a popped task may still be executing.
   433	//   2. Publish PREPARING, rewrite all entries while routing still resolves to the old owner, and
   434	//      settle owner-local bookkeeping while both loops remain quiescent.
   435	//   3. Publish COMMITTED once. Only then may the new owner touch the shard's store. A producer that
   436	//      had already read the old route is forwarded by the old owner before shard access.
   437	//
   438	// Skipping step 2 puts two threads in one FlatStore, which has no locks precisely because that is
   439	// supposed to be impossible — it would corrupt silently rather than crash.
   440	//
   441	// Written as a contract rather than an implementation because there is no LB yet and a half-built
   442	// migration path is worse than none.
   443	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

   445	    int32_t  shard_id    = -1;
   446	    uint32_t from_thread = 0;
   447	    uint32_t to_thread   = 0;
   448	    size_t   cost_bytes  = 0;    // what the new domain must re-pull; Shard::migration_cost_bytes()
   449	};

   757	    // its new flush frontier, so every append below is on a frame boundary.
   758	    bool flush_deferred_oob(Client& conn) {
   759	        if (__builtin_expect(oob_defer_.empty(), true)) return false;
   760	        auto found = oob_defer_.find(&conn);
   761	        if (found == oob_defer_.end()) return false;
   762	        const uint64_t retired_through = conn.rob().flush_id();
   763	        DeferredOobQueue& queue = found->second;
   764	        bool flushed = false;
   765	        while (!queue.empty() && queue.front().after <= retired_through) {
   766	            conn.append_oob(queue.front().bytes.data(), queue.front().bytes.size());
   767	            queue.pop_front();
   768	            flushed = true;
   769	        }
   770	        if (queue.empty()) oob_defer_.erase(found);
   771	        return flushed;
   772	    }

   754	// Variants 1 and 3 permit concurrent Raw overwrite/copy. Their sequence rejects a torn logical
   755	// snapshot, while the relaxed atomic accesses below make the payload access itself legal C++.
   756	// Cell geometry depends only on the immutable value address and allocation class, never on a
   757	// changing length: full aligned words carry the body and only unaligned allocation edges use byte
   758	// atomics. Constructors and every non-overwrite build retain their original memcpy path.

   761	        static_assert(std::atomic_ref<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free,
   762	                      "variant A requires a lock-free atomic Raw length");
   763	        static_assert(std::atomic_ref<uint32_t>::required_alignment <= alignof(KvObj),
   764	                      "variant A requires KvObj to align its atomic Raw length");
   765	        return std::atomic_ref<const uint32_t>(object->vlen).load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
   766	    }
   767	    return object->raw_length_relaxed();
   768	}

   137	// Allocated only for the boot-armed fused read-local lane. The Server keeps only one pointer at its
   138	// true tail, so baseline member offsets and cache-line sharing remain unchanged.
   139	struct ReadLocalServerState {
   140	    std::atomic<uint64_t> epoch{1};
   141	};
   142	
   143	// A snapshot/placement drain is the only reader, while opens and closes happen on unrelated
   144	// physical threads.  Monotonic halves avoid the false-zero a signed per-thread delta can expose
   145	// when a scan observes an executor's close before the admitting IO's open.  Cache-line spacing
   146	// keeps those writers independent.
   147	struct alignas(64) AtomicApplySlot {
   148	    std::atomic<uint64_t> opened{0};
   149	    std::atomic<uint64_t> closed{0};
   150	};
   151	static_assert(sizeof(AtomicApplySlot) == 64);
   152	static_assert(alignof(AtomicApplySlot) == 64);

   161	
   162	    // Resolve placement and the shard default once, before AOF/snapshot recovery reads geometry.
   163	    bool prepare_boot(Config& cfg) {
   164	        const char* domains = std::getenv("TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS");
   165	        if (domains && *domains) {
   166	            if (!topo_.declare(domains)) {
   167	                std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS '%s' invalid\n", domains);
   168	                return false;
   169	            }
   170	        } else if (!topo_.discover()) {
   171	            std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: could not discover any allowed cpu\n");
   172	            return false;
   173	        }
   174	        if (!topo_.discover_thread_siblings()) {
   175	            std::fprintf(stderr, "fatal: could not read Linux thread_siblings_list topology\n");
   176	            return false;
   177	        }
   178	        smt_mode_ = topo_.allowed_sibling_pairs() != 0;
   179	        bool placed = false;
   180	        if (cfg.thread_mode == ThreadMode::Fused) {
   181	            placed = placement_.build_fused(topo_, cfg.place);
   182	        } else {
   183	            // Default shape: an even io/ex split of every allowed cpu, io taking the odd one out --
   184	            // the measured 2s center (4:4-class) generalized to any core count.
   185	            uint32_t di = cfg.even_ifid, de = cfg.even_ex;
   186	            if (!cfg.place && !(di | de)) {
   187	                uint32_t n = 0;
   188	                for (uint32_t d = 0; d < topo_.ndomains(); d++)
   189	                    n += static_cast<uint32_t>(topo_.cpus_in(d).size());
   190	                if (smt_mode_) {
   191	                    n = 2 * topo_.allowed_sibling_pairs();
   192	                    de = (n / 4) * 2;
   193	                } else de = n / 2;
   194	                di = n - de;
   195	            }
   196	            placed = cfg.place
   197	                ? placement_.build_explicit(topo_, cfg.place)
   198	                : placement_.build_even(topo_, di, de, smt_mode_ != 0);
   199	        }
   200	        if (!placed) return false;
   201	        if (!placement_.configure_smt_units(topo_, smt_mode_ != 0)) return false;
   202	        if (!placement_.reserve_runtime_roles(placement_.total_threads())) return false;
   203	        if (placement_.ifid_threads().empty() || placement_.ex_threads().empty()) {
   204	            std::fprintf(stderr, "placement needs at least one ifid and one ex thread\n");
   205	            return false;
   206	        }
   207	        if (cfg.shards == Config::kShardsAuto)
   208	            cfg.shards = cfg_default_shards(static_cast<uint32_t>(placement_.ex_threads().size()));
   209	        return true;
   210	    }

Author: henry <henrychen917@protonmail.com>
Date:   Mon Aug 24 10:13:53 2026 +0800

    delete 3s: pure 2s is the base (owner ruling, evidence-backed) + Op repack to 336B
    
    (Recommitted: the first attempt fce1a7a lost the deletion to an unpopped
    git stash from the bisect's binary builds and committed only the repack
    under this message. Working-tree recovered from stash@{0}, repack re-applied,
    combined tree re-validated: sizeof(Op)=336, 3s spellings rejected, smoke 6/6,
    64c dual anchor vs pre-direct = wash.)
    
    The evidence that decided it: depth sweep 64c (3s vs 2s: -33% p1 -> +4% p32,
    crossover ~p16-32); 3s's one win was +2.0% GET / +4.1% SET at 64c p32;
    overload REFUTED post-2s-fix (2s +8%, half the tail); large values tied at
    the 25GbE wall. Deleted: wb_loop.h, Role::Wb, WbProto/WbGuard/link mutex,
    per-conn sender_thread, needs_io_wake, remote teardown handshake, sender
    pairing, --send-target, wb arity of --spread/--ratio/--place.
    Repack: kInlineReply 128->112 pays for the direct-reply fields (the 352B Op
    measured -3.7% at 64c p32; at the DRAM wall, ROB footprint is throughput).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0131nXyQ5SvYWSgqqkHefHVb

     1	# Armed local-read capture-at-prefetch audit
     2	
     3	> Historical research record: configuration recipes and measurements below describe earlier
     4	> revisions. Deleted controls are not accepted by the merged server, and the manual-map
     5	> dispatch-scaling instrument is retired. For current controls and merge dispositions, see
     6	> [DESIGN-KNOBS.md](DESIGN-KNOBS.md) and [MERGE.md](MERGE.md).
     7	
     8	Baseline: `b7fd92c0736618c719f29d0202aea009edc6adcb`.
     9	
    10	## Phase 1 finding: execute reloads the slot
    11	
    12	The armed point-read batch in `ExLoopT::drain_local_reads()` has separate prefetch and execute
    13	walks, but the prefetch walk does not retain a lookup result.  `FlatStore::read_local_prefetch()`
    14	only snapshots eligible table topology and issues a hardware hint for each table's home slot.  The
    15	later `prepare_local_read()` call invokes `FlatStore::read_local_probe()`, whose open-addressing
    16	walk acquire-loads the slot words at execute time and selects the `KvObj` then.
    17	
    18	Consequently, a plain cross-client writer can replace a prefetched slot between those walks.  Such
    19	an immutable-object replacement deliberately does not advance the read-local table generation, so
    20	execute accepts the newer pointer and can stall on an object that the batch did not prefetch.  The
    21	same shape exists inside MGET for its at-most-32-key prefetch window.
    22	
    23	This is not an ordering requirement.  Parser-side write-ring and owner-tail conflict checks keep a
    24	connection's own unresolved writes out of the local execution path.  A read racing only another
    25	connection's committed replacement may place its read cut before that replacement and serve the
    26	already-observed immutable object.
    27	
    28	## Capture constraints
    29	
    30	Capture must perform the complete validated probe at prefetch time, not retain only the home word:
    31	linear probing must still skip tombstones and tag/key mismatches, stop at empty, and search the
    32	current table before the old table.  The capture therefore consists of the observed slot address,
    33	the `KvObj` pointer decoded from that slot (or a miss), and the store publication generation.
    34	Execute may read the captured object directly but must not reload the slot.
    35	
    36	The capture is safe only as stack-local state for one bounded local-drain call.  Every such call
    37	runs inside the fused pass's rotation boundary; its `ThreadCtx` tick is published only after the pass
    38	returns.  Writers unlink first and defer both displaced objects and retired tables until every
    39	active participant publishes a tick newer than the retirement stamp.  Thus the captured slot/table
    40	and object remain allocated through execute, while the final publication validation still rejects
    41	an open atomic group, table resize/move, bulk clear, or ownership handoff.  Plain object replacement,
    42	DEL, and TTL replacement leave that generation unchanged and may legally be observed on either
    43	side of the read cut.
    44	
    45	Every later batch must probe and capture afresh; no capture may be stored in the persistent local
    46	lane or survive a rotation boundary.  Stable misses retain their existing command behavior: GET
    47	demotes to the owner, while MGET emits a nil element.
    48	
    49	## Phase 2 implementation
    50	
    51	`--read-local-prefetch-capture 1` (the default) keeps the legacy home-slot hint pass, then captures
    52	the exact result of a complete open-address probe: result, slot address, decoded immutable `KvObj`
    53	pointer, and publication state.  Execute copies from that captured object without loading through
    54	the slot.  `--read-local-prefetch-capture 0` selects the old hint-only prefetch plus execute-time
    55	probe for A/B measurement.
    56	
    57	Point-only client chunks use three passes so slot and object latency can overlap across the batch:
    58	I0 hints home words, C0 captures and hints the selected objects/values, and E0 copies the captured
    59	versions.  Mixed GET/MGET chunks capture and consume commands in connection order.  MGET processes
    60	arbitrary key counts in bounded 32-key I0/C0/E0 windows and rebuilds all of its window captures on
    61	an internal retry.  All capture buffers are stack locals inside the bounded drain and are gone
    62	before the enclosing rotation publishes its QSBR tick.
    63	
    64	The post-copy publication validation remains unchanged in purpose.  It rejects pending atomic work
    65	and completed pending-bit intervals, table resize/move, clear, and ownership changes, while stable
    66	immutable SET/DEL/TTL slot swaps remain intentionally invisible.  Same-connection write-ring and
    67	owner-tail gates continue to keep RYOW reads out of this local path; only cross-client publication
    68	can replace a captured object between C0 and E0.

    73	// co-locate both in byte zero, freeing the old encoding byte for Raw's bounded (<=192) length. The
    74	// aligned word at offset four is then a full, non-wrapping object sequence for Raw; flags and key
    75	// length retain their old offsets, and other encodings retain the original 32-bit vlen meaning.
    76	// All other selectors preserve the complete original byte layout.

    78	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3

    80	    uint8_t  enc : 2;   // Enc needs 0..3
    81	    uint8_t  type_enc_spare : 3;
    82	    uint8_t  raw_vlen;  // Enc::Raw only; all other encodings leave this zero
    83	    uint8_t  flags;     // KvObjFlags
    84	    uint8_t  klen8;     // key length when < 255; 255 means "see the u32 after the header"
    85	    union {
    86	        uint32_t vlen;         // non-Raw inline/external length
    87	        uint32_t raw_sequence; // Enc::Raw odd/even publication sequence
    88	    };
    89	#else
    90	    uint8_t  type;      // Type
    91	    uint8_t  enc;       // Enc

    94	    uint32_t vlen;      // inline value length, or external length when Enc::Extern
    95	#endif

   402	    void seal_pending() {
   403	        if (!ring_.unsealed) return;
   404	        // Every object/table in the suffix was unlinked before this seq-cst RMW. The returned old
   405	        // epoch is therefore a valid common retirement stamp for the entire owner-pass batch --
   406	        // recorded once, not once per entry.

   410	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats& stats = settax_stats();
   411	        stats.qsbr_seals++;
   412	        stats.qsbr_sealed_entries += sealed;
   413	#endif
   414	    }

   416	    void force_oldest_grace() {
   417	        // The freeing thread is also a QSBR participant. It has finished this rotation's local-read
   418	        // copy before owner mutation can reach here, so publishing its current epoch is the safe
   419	        // point that prevents a full list from waiting on itself.
   420	        seal_pending();
   421	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   422	        settax_stats().qsbr_forced_graces++;
   423	#endif
   424	        while (ring_.full()) {
   425	            // Preserve a permanent/parked publication if shutdown cleanup reaches this path.
   426	            owner_->refresh_read_local_quiescence(server_->read_local_epoch());
   427	            if (!drain_ready()) {
   428	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   429	                settax_stats().qsbr_forced_yields++;
   430	#endif
   431	                __builtin_ia32_pause();
   432	                ::sched_yield();
   433	            }
   434	        }
   435	    }

12:## One-to-one knob accounting
22:| `--read-local-prefetch-capture` | `1` | Deleted; capture selected statically | Preserve the winning immutable-object capture at prefetch. |
23:| `--read-local-atomic-filter` | `1` | Deleted; precise filter whenever read-local is armed | Preserve the winning per-key safety filter, including fail-closed poison and overflow handling. |
24:| `--read-local-interleave` | `1` | Deleted; bounded interleave whenever read-local is armed | Preserve bounded local chunks and per-producer owner quanta. |
28:| `--smt-mode` | `0` | Deleted; derive from complete sibling pairs in the allowed topology | Use existing sibling-unit placement and FLIP invariants when pairs are present. |
29:| `--genthread-schedule` | No independent default; compatibility alias | Deleted | Remove the alias that assigned fused mode and an overlap value. See objection about the original “zero uses” premise. |
38:| `--key-lb` | `1` | Collapsed into `--lb` | One switch controls key and client balancing together. |
39:| `--client-lb` | `1` | Collapsed into `--lb` | Same switch; no independently disabled half remains. |
43:| `--lb-imbalance-pct` | `25` | Collapsed; twice measured quiet jitter | Separate key/client learners; excursions cannot enlarge their own admission band. |
46:| No `--lb` | — | **`--lb 0\|1`, default `1`** | The sole public key/client balancing switch; `0` allocates no LB sidecar, bucket counters/census arrays, or controller windows. |
48:| `--ratio` | Unset; even split | Kept, split only | Global IO/EX counts, spread over locality domains; retain conf/CLI precedence with `place`. |
49:| `--place` | Derived | Kept, derived by default | Explicit `role@cpu` selection remains; fused mode uses labels only as CPU selectors. |
51:| `--read-local` | `0` | Kept, `0\|1` | Effective only in fused plain scheduling; inactive modes retain ordinary owner dispatch. |
55:| `--overlap` | `0` | **`--x-overlap 0\|1\|2`**, default `0` | Study namespace only; same schedules and mode/engine validation. |

    38	    uint64_t total = 0;
    39	    for (uint64_t value : input) total += value;
    40	    if (!total) return;
    41	    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++)
    42	        output[i] = static_cast<double>(input[i]) / static_cast<double>(total);
    43	}

    45	void add_delta(uint64_t current, uint64_t previous, uint64_t& destination) {
    46	    if (current >= previous) destination += current - previous;

    51	FlipSignature flip_signature(const FlipFingerprintWindow& sample) {
    52	    FlipSignature signature;
    53	    if (!sample.commands) return signature;
    54	    normalize(sample.pass_depth, signature.pass_depth);
    55	    normalize(sample.command_class, signature.command_class);
    56	    signature.keys_per_multikey = sample.multikey_ops
    57	        ? static_cast<double>(sample.multikey_keys) / sample.multikey_ops : 0;
    58	    signature.value_bytes_per_command =
    59	        static_cast<double>(sample.value_bytes) / sample.commands;
    60	    signature.commands = sample.commands;
    61	    signature.valid = true;
    62	    return signature;
    63	}
    64	
    65	double flip_signature_distance(const FlipSignature& left, const FlipSignature& right) {
    66	    if (!left.valid || !right.valid) return 0;
    67	    double class_l1 = 0;
    68	    for (size_t i = 0; i < left.command_class.size(); i++)
    69	        class_l1 += std::abs(left.command_class[i] - right.command_class[i]);
    70	    // Three families, all of them properties of WHAT THE CLIENTS ASKED FOR: the command-class mix,
    71	    // the keys each multi-key command names, and the value bytes each command carries. The
    72	    // probability-vector L1 is in [0,2] and each relative scalar distance is in [0,1], so dividing
    73	    // by the family count keeps the distance normalized to [0,1].
    74	    //
    75	    // pass_depth is NOT here. Measured on the multi-key regime this defect was found in: one
    76	    // controller step from io=5 to io=7 moved the pass-depth distance by 0.0476 -- eight to forty
    77	    // times its own learned trigger band -- while the three mix families moved by 4.2e-7, 0 and
    78	    // 5.4e-7 across the same seconds. Parse-pass occupancy describes how the io threads happened
    79	    // to batch arrivals, which is exactly what the actuator changes when it moves connections
    80	    // between owners. Judging placement with it is the sweep-abandon livelock: the controller
    81	    // re-fires on its own last move. Pipeline-depth changes that matter still reach the controller
    82	    // through the rate detector, which owns volume.
    83	    return (class_l1 * 0.5 +
    84	            unit_normalized_distance(left.keys_per_multikey, right.keys_per_multikey) +
    85	            unit_normalized_distance(left.value_bytes_per_command,
    86	                                     right.value_bytes_per_command)) / 3.0;
    87	}
    88	
    89	double flip_signature_pass_distance(const FlipSignature& left, const FlipSignature& right) {
    90	    if (!left.valid || !right.valid) return 0;
    91	    double pass_l1 = 0;
    92	    for (size_t i = 0; i < left.pass_depth.size(); i++)
    93	        pass_l1 += std::abs(left.pass_depth[i] - right.pass_depth[i]);
    94	    return pass_l1 * 0.5;
    95	}

   111	void FlipShiftDetector::update_band() {
   112	    if (configured_band_ == 0) {
   113	        band_ = 0;
   114	        return;
   115	    }
   116	    // SAMPLING SCALE, not counting resolution. Every family in the distance is a proportion or a
   117	    // per-command mean estimated from the N commands this window observed, so two windows drawn
   118	    // from one stationary workload differ by the ESTIMATOR'S OWN NOISE, which falls as 1/sqrt(N)
   119	    // -- never as 1/N. A Bernoulli proportion's standard error is at most 0.5/sqrt(N) and the
   120	    // difference of two independent estimates at most sqrt(2) of that, so 1/sqrt(N) bounds the
   121	    // per-family noise with room for the few terms an L1 sums. The old 1/N quantum understated it
   122	    // by sqrt(N) -- twentyfold at 13.5k commands a window -- which is how a window that merely
   123	    // drew 60 MSETs where the last one drew 50 could read as a workload change. A window that
   124	    // observed no commands supplies no evidence: saturate at one command (quantum 1.0) instead of
   125	    // collapsing to zero, or an anchor cut from an idle window freezes a zero band and judges the
   126	    // first busy wobble as a mix shift. Rate triggers, not fingerprints, own idle->busy.
   127	    //
   128	    // N IS WHAT THE SIGNATURE WAS ESTIMATED FROM, so when the writer samples the request stream the
   129	    // quantum grows with the sampling: at one command in a hundred a 100-command window resolves
   130	    // the mix to about 0.1, not to the 0.009 the underlying 10k commands would give.
   131	    const double quantum =
   132	        1.0 / std::sqrt(static_cast<double>(std::max<uint64_t>(smoothed_.commands, 1)));
   133	    // A TYPED BAND IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING, AND IT CANNOT BUY RESOLUTION THE SIGNAL HAS NOT GOT.
   134	    // The internal detector's explicit-band unit-test control sets the mix change worth a maneuver;
   135	    // it says nothing about how
   136	    // still the signature holds, and it used to return here consulting neither the estimator's
   137	    // resolution nor the signal's measured movement. Measured by the gate-hygiene lane on a driver
   138	    // whose rate held to 0.07% across 34 samples: a fingerprint distance of 0.2518 against a flat
   139	    // 0.0200 band -- 12.6x -- fired a maneuver on a stationary load. Simulated here on a 1-in-100
   140	    // sampled stream, a typed 2% band produced three two-consecutive exceedances in 600 stationary
   141	    // windows (a spurious maneuver each); with the quantum applied it produces none, and a real mix
   142	    // change still clears the band by 3.3x. So both branches take the same two floors.
   143	    const double floor = std::max(2.0 * quantum, signature_noise_.bound());
   144	    if (configured_band_ > 0) {
   145	        band_ = std::max(static_cast<double>(configured_band_) / 100.0, floor);
   146	        return;
   147	    }
   148	    // ... and the learned band adds the frozen learning-window jitter, floored the same way: that
   149	    // jitter is the largest adjacent step seen in the few windows before the anchor, so a learning
   150	    // window that happened to be still freezes a band the hold then trips over.
   151	    band_ = std::max(2.0 * jitter_, floor);
   152	}

   231	bool FlipController::init(bool enabled, int32_t configured_band, uint32_t nthreads) {
   232	    enabled_ = enabled;
   233	    configured_band_ = configured_band;
   234	    signature_learning_windows_ = std::max<uint32_t>(1, nthreads);
   235	    maneuver_learning_windows_ = 0;
   236	    for (uint32_t value = nthreads; value > 1; value >>= 1)
   237	        maneuver_learning_windows_++;
   238	    maneuver_learning_windows_ = std::max<uint32_t>(1, maneuver_learning_windows_);
   239	    // The signature noise estimate's time constant is the same window count the controller already
   240	    // uses to learn a signature at an anchor -- derived from the live pool, not typed.
   241	    shift_detector_ = FlipShiftDetector(configured_band, signature_learning_windows_);
   242	    if (!enabled) {
   243	        phase_ = Phase::Disabled;
   244	        return true;
   245	    }
   246	    try {
   247	        fingerprint_last_.resize(nthreads);
   248	        maneuver_start_.resize(nthreads);
   249	        maneuver_mark_.resize(nthreads);
   250	        // At most one observation per split is needed for the seek itself, followed by up to one
   251	        // thread-count-derived set of final anchor readings. Reserve both cold phases up front.
   252	        readings_.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(nthreads) * 2);
   253	    } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
   254	        return false;
   255	    }
   256	    phase_ = Phase::BootPending;
   257	    return true;
   258	}

I found a correctness issue beside the handoff cleanup: shard notification state still points at the old owner until a later executor pass. The target is a plain `bool`, and execution can resume before it is rebound. I’m checking the event path and will report this separately from the vestigial findings.

    28	## Capture constraints
    29	
    30	Capture must perform the complete validated probe at prefetch time, not retain only the home word:
    31	linear probing must still skip tombstones and tag/key mismatches, stop at empty, and search the
    32	current table before the old table.  The capture therefore consists of the observed slot address,
    33	the `KvObj` pointer decoded from that slot (or a miss), and the store publication generation.
    34	Execute may read the captured object directly but must not reload the slot.
    35	
    36	The capture is safe only as stack-local state for one bounded local-drain call.  Every such call
    37	runs inside the fused pass's rotation boundary; its `ThreadCtx` tick is published only after the pass
    38	returns.  Writers unlink first and defer both displaced objects and retired tables until every
    39	active participant publishes a tick newer than the retirement stamp.  Thus the captured slot/table
    40	and object remain allocated through execute, while the final publication validation still rejects
    41	an open atomic group, table resize/move, bulk clear, or ownership handoff.  Plain object replacement,

**VESTIGIAL.md — read-only survey**

Audited checkout: `c8e61f646`. Source and history inspection only; no build, server, benchmark, gate, or test execution. No files were written. The pre-existing modification to `CODEX-OUT.md` remains untouched.

The strongest opportunities remove obsolete choices from atomic admission, send handling, and read-local writes. A separate ownership race surfaced while tracing the handoff machinery; it is described after the ranked findings.

Two scope discrepancies matter:

- Fused `overlap` still accepts **0, 1, and 2**. Values 1 and 2 select distinct schedules; the retired implementation is the old streams scheduler. See [config.h:632](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:632) and [io_loop.h:526](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:526).
- In-place build selectors **1 and 3 remain supported**, and the checkout’s `Config` layout assertion is **528 bytes**, versus the supplied 624-byte lock. See [read_local_settax.h:29](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/read_local_settax.h:29) and [config.h:365](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/config.h:365).

Estimates below describe source simplification and field storage. They are approximate, exclude wholesale deletion of unreachable implementations, and make no throughput claim. Compiler-folded choices are identified explicitly.

**1. SIMPLIFY — Atomic admission still supports a mutable, unlimited window**

Sites: [server.h:2473](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2473), [server.h:2541](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2541), [server.h:3311](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3311).

The live admission and retirement paths repeatedly load `atomic_window()` and handle zero as unlimited. Neither variation survives: boot validates `shards` in `1..256`, then installs `min(16 * shards, 1024)`, always positive. The only subsequent window store republishes the same value.

The link is explicit in [DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/DESIGN-KNOBS.md:30): `--atomic-window` and its live setter were deleted. Nevertheless, `atomic_reconfigure_credits(uint32_t window)` retains its parameter, same-value publication, and zero-window arithmetic.

Collapse to a boot-derived ordinary value, remove the reconfiguration parameter and repeated publication, and make credit admission/return unconditional with respect to window existence.

**Value:** approximately 15–25 lines; four operation-path window-load sites and five associated conditional terms become unnecessary. The credit-generation handshake, lease accounting, snapshot barrier, and live `atomic` toggle still have consumers and must remain.

**2. SIMPLIFY — Serving writeback engines still accept missing infrastructure**

Sites: [wb.h:124](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:124), [wb.h:197](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:197), [wb.h:807](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:807), [wb.h:1049](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/wb.h:1049).

`WbEngine::bind()` defaults release, retirement, output-limit, clock, and signal hooks to null. Send and retirement paths consequently keep checking whether those facilities exist.

Every engine that actually serves connections is bound by [io_loop.h:104](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:104), which supplies all of them. The sole incomplete binding belongs to the never-serving executor engine in finding 8, retained after `exwb` deletion.

Require complete binding for a serving engine and remove pointer-presence checks. Preserve the actual output-limit enabled value, callback results, and callback indirections; those still perform useful work.

**Value:** roughly 20–30 redundant pointer-presence tests across send/retirement variants, including tests within operation retirement. This removes optionality, not the callback mechanism itself.

**3. SIMPLIFY — Executor-slot translation is an identity lookup**

Sites: [server.h:296](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:296), [server.h:2121](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:2121), [server.h:3508](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:3508).

Boot fills `executor_slots_[tid] = tid` for every physical thread and never changes the table. Atomic, MULTI, and scatter-gather paths still consult it at eight source call sites, including [atomics_glue.inc:217](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:217).

History establishes the obsolete design precisely: commit `3ca2c450e` replaced dense indexing over a fixed executor subset with stable physical-thread indexing for FLIP, but retained the translation table.

Replace the accessor with a bounded identity operation, preserving the existing invalid-thread result. Validated callers can use the physical thread ID directly.

**Value:** 128 bytes of mapping storage, two initialization loops, and one dependent lookup per accessor invocation. Approximately 10–20 lines. This is residue of fixed-role executor numbering, not `exmajor`.

**4. SIMPLIFY — RYOW writes still test for an impossible ring-capacity overflow**

Sites: [rob.h:505](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:505), [rob.h:538](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:538), [rob.h:1012](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/net/rob.h:1012).

Both refinement functions test `write_count == kWriteRingCapacity`. Commit-side resolution repeats the test and converts the connection to a conservative generation.

The original ring was independently bounded at 16 entries: commit `f9080c9ca`. It is now sized to the ROB window. **Correctness exceptions discovered during the survey**

These are outside the deletion ranking.

**Ownership race: notification adoption still happens after execution resumes.**  
The LB commit publishes `Idle` at [server.h:1407](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1407) after moving shards. The transfer updates the read-local retire sink but does not update `Shard::notify_pending_`.

The destination repairs notification pointers later at [ex_loop.h:1858](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858). Both fused and split execution can drain tasks before reaching that repair: [ex_loop.h:549](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:549) and [ex_loop.h:759](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:759).

A resumed command that expires or evicts a key enters the keyless event route at [notify.inc:427](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/notify.inc:427), which eventually calls [shard.h:166](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/shard.h:166). That writes through the stale pointer into the previous owner’s **plain bool**, while that owner can independently read/write it.

This is a source-level cross-owner data-race path and violates the requirement to move per-owner bindings within the ownership critical section. The later forced drain can recover notification discovery; it cannot repair the missing synchronization. Notification binding needs adoption before resume. This was not reproduced by execution.

**Armed read-local still contains reader retries and topology seqlock validation.**  
[ex_loop.h:1295](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1295) sets captured MGET attempts to two, and [ex_loop.h:1431](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1431) records retrying before the next attempt. This remains live in the default build when read-local is armed.

Default probes also validate an odd/even topology sequence: [flatstore.h:3337](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3337), with writer brackets at [flatstore.h:3494](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3494). Under the supplied prohibition on per-operation seqlocks, that is another contract conflict. These protections currently prevent torn topology observations; deleting them as cleanup would weaken correctness.

**Selectable overwrite variants violate the armed in-place-write prohibition.**  
Selectors 1 and 3 explicitly overwrite published raw values at [flatstore.h:2758](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2758) and [flatstore.h:2784](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2784). Selector 3 also supplies the failed-validation route that can retry point reads. The unqualified selector-0 build retains immutable replacement.

- Task reservation remains live in read-local demotion at [io_loop.h:3705](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:3705).

- Atomic-window stalls, cache statistics, and LB movement counters still report varying mechanisms. The established always-zero diagnostic contribution is the executor `WbEngine` in finding 8.

Audited checkout: `c8e61f646`. Source and history inspection only; no build, server, benchmark, gate, or test execution. No files were written. The pre-existing modification to `CODEX-OUT.md` remains untouched.

The strongest opportunities remove obsolete choices from atomic admission, send handling, and read-local writes. A separate ownership race surfaced while tracing the handoff machinery; it is described after the ranked findings.

**Correctness exceptions discovered during the survey**

These are outside the deletion ranking.

**Ownership race: notification adoption still happens after execution resumes.**  
The LB commit publishes `Idle` at [server.h:1407](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:1407) after moving shards. The transfer updates the read-local retire sink but does not update `Shard::notify_pending_`.

The destination repairs notification pointers later at [ex_loop.h:1858](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858). Both fused and split execution can drain tasks before reaching that repair: [ex_loop.h:549](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:549) and [ex_loop.h:759](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:759).

A resumed command that expires or evicts a key enters the keyless event route at [notify.inc:427](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/notify.inc:427), which eventually calls [shard.h:166](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/shard.h:166). That writes through the stale pointer into the previous owner’s **plain bool**, while that owner can independently read/write it.

This is a source-level cross-owner data-race path and violates the requirement to move per-owner bindings within the ownership critical section. The later forced drain can recover notification discovery; it cannot repair the missing synchronization. Notification binding needs adoption before resume. This was not reproduced by execution.

**Armed read-local still contains reader retries and topology seqlock validation.**  
[ex_loop.h:1295](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1295) sets captured MGET attempts to two, and [ex_loop.h:1431](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/ex_loop.h:1431) records retrying before the next attempt. This remains live in the default build when read-local is armed.

Default probes also validate an odd/even topology sequence: [flatstore.h:3337](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3337), with writer brackets at [flatstore.h:3494](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:3494). Under the supplied prohibition on per-operation seqlocks, that is another contract conflict. These protections currently prevent torn topology observations; deleting them as cleanup would weaken correctness.

**Selectable overwrite variants violate the armed in-place-write prohibition.**  
Selectors 1 and 3 explicitly overwrite published raw values at [flatstore.h:2758](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2758) and [flatstore.h:2784](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/store/flatstore.h:2784). Selector 3 also supplies the failed-validation route that can retry point reads. The unqualified selector-0 build retains immutable replacement.

**Tempting cuts that lack the required proof**

- The unreachable streams loop and uncalled executor wrappers are dead-code candidates. Their full bodies are excluded from these estimates; findings 7 and 11 concern machinery they left on surviving paths.
- Task reservation remains live in read-local demotion at [io_loop.h:3705](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/io_loop.h:3705).
- Ready-slot exhaustion remains live at [thread.h:1055](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/thread.h:1055), requiring the claimed notification channel and its lifetime protections.
- SMT remains topology-dependent, and `TOMOKV_L3_DOMAINS` remains an explicit environment override: [server.h:164](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/core/server.h:164).
- No confirmed executing residue was tied specifically to `connalloc` or `exmajor`. Current owner-grouped scatter posting still creates one task per shard fragment: [scatter_engine.inc:1246](/home/user/Projects/cx-vestigial/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:1246).
- Atomic-window stalls, cache statistics, and LB movement counters still report varying mechanisms. The established always-zero diagnostic contribution is the executor `WbEngine` in finding 8.
